title: 13 Best PMS for Airbnb Hosts to Manage More in 2026
summary: Find the best PMS for Airbnb hosts in 2026 and see how AI agents help property managers scale faster without burning out their team.
body_text: Every PMS promises scale. Most stop working the moment a guest goes off-script. Here is what to look for, what to ignore, and the gap no calendar sync will ever close. A property manager juggling five listings can survive on Airbnb's native tools, a shared inbox, and a lot of caffeine. Add ten more and the math changes fast: calendars multiply, cleaning crews need coordination, and guest messages arrive at hours no one planned to work. Most vacation rental property managers and operations leads think that if they pick the right PMS with the best built-in messaging automation, they can scale their portfolio without hiring more staff or burning out their current team. That's the moment most operators start researching Airbnb property management software , and the moment the category's real limits start to matter. Understanding what a PMS actually does, and where it stops, is the decision that separates operators who scale cleanly from those who scale into chaos. An Airbnb PMS is a centralized operations hub. See our AI for hospitality for how this works in practice. It consolidates calendars, automates scheduled messages, triggers cleaning tasks, and tracks owner reporting across every listing in one dashboard. According to industry research, property management companies oversee an average of 497 units per company, which makes a centralized system a structural necessity, not a luxury. Without one, coordination overhead alone consumes the margin. What a PMS was never designed to do is hold an unscripted conversation. When a guest asks whether the parking space fits an oversized truck, or reports a broken heater mid-stay, the PMS delivers that message to an inbox, then waits. Resolution still depends on a human reading, deciding, and typing a reply. The essential features of an Airbnb PMS are: Unified inbox (all OTA messages in one place) Automated scheduled messaging (check-in instructions, review requests, departure reminders) Calendar and channel sync Cleaning and maintenance task triggers Owner reporting Airbnb's own Software Partners program lists vetted PMS integrations meeting its API standards, a useful starting filter when evaluating platforms. These five features eliminate the coordination overhead that otherwise eats team hours. They handle everything predictable: known touchpoints, fixed sequences, scheduled workflows. 497 average units managed per property company Key takeaways A PMS organizes your calendar, coordinates your cleaners, and fires scheduled templates, it does not hold a live conversation with a guest locked out at 11 PM. Automated check-in and checkout messages quiet the inbox at scale, but unscripted mid-stay questions arrive outside every template sequence, often overnight, and that gap is where review scores actually move. Why Manual Guest Messaging Breaks Down as Your Airbnb Portfolio Grows Turning on automated check-in and checkout messages feels like solving the communication problem. Most vacation rental property managers and operations leads think: "If I pick the right PMS with the best built-in messaging automation , I can scale my portfolio without hiring more staff or burning out my current team." The inbox quiets down, the templates fire on schedule, and the operation looks manageable, until the portfolio grows past a handful of properties and the gaps between those templates start filling with questions no sequence was ever built to answer. The reality is more specific than "message volume gets high." Hosts managing even a single property face a constant stream of guest questions, many asking about information already covered in the listing or arrival guide. As the portfolio grows, that stream becomes a flood no manual process can reliably absorb. What makes it worse is the friction baked into every response: staff open the PMS, locate the reservation, then compose a reply, a multi-step process slower than a phone call for something as simple as confirming a checkout time. The process defeats the purpose of messaging entirely. Conduit Agents are most beneficial: businesses receiving a high volume of repetitive guest messages that already have existing documentation, SOPs, FAQs, property manuals, ready to train an agent on. "Manual messaging consumed 20+ minutes per booking, a burden that compounds significantly as my portfolio size grows." Each New Listing Compounds Message Volume Faster Than Headcount Can Keep Up The math is straightforward and brutal. A single vacation rental booking generates multiple guest touchpoints across the stay arc: pre-arrival questions, mid-stay requests, and post-checkout follow-ups. Multiply that across 15 or 20 listings and the daily message volume stops being a communication task and starts being a full-time job. Operators who have managed this manually describe spending 20 or more minutes per booking just on routine exchanges, WiFi passwords, early check-in requests, parking instructions. These are not novel questions; they are the same questions repeated for every guest, across every property, on every booking. The cycle is draining by design, and it compounds directly with booking volume. Adding a property means adding message volume immediately; adding a team member means weeks of hiring and onboarding. The gap between those two timelines is where response quality quietly erodes, and where missed messages between guests and cleaning staff begin to slip through, a problem that grows more acute with every listing added. Conduit's AI Agents are designed to close that gap. Once connected to your existing SOPs and property manuals, without requiring manual re-entry if your documentation already lives in tools like Notion or Google Drive, the agent can deliver its first automated guest reply within days. The operations team then uses the Inbox to monitor, review, and manage all conversations the AI agent is handling on an ongoing basis, maintaining visibility without being the first line of response for every routine inquiry. The Overnight Gap - How Response Times Drain Review Scores and Booking Conversion Airbnb requires hosts to maintain a 90% or higher response rate within 24 hours to qualify for Superhost status. That threshold is achievable at five properties with a disciplined team. At 20 properties, it demands someone watching the inbox at 2 a.m. on a Tuesday. Airbnb's guidance also confirms that response time directly affects search ranking and booking conversion, meaning the overnight gap is not just a guest experience problem, it is a revenue problem that compounds silently, booking by booking, until the review score reflects it. Conduit.ai Agents respond continuously, before, during, or after a stay, whenever a guest sends a message. That coverage is not limited to business hours or staffed shifts. It is the specific capability that closes the overnight gap without requiring a team member to be on call, and it addresses the core Airbnb compliance risk that grows harder to manage manually as portfolio size increases. Inconsistent Reply Quality Across Listings Is What Triggers Negative Reviews The review risk is not slow replies alone, it is inconsistent replies. A guest at one property receives a prompt, detailed reply from an operations lead who knows the unit well; a guest at another property sends the same question on a busy night and waits three hours. Airbnb guests leave star ratings based on that experience, and inconsistent reply quality across a growing portfolio is one of the clearest predictors of review score variance that operators cannot see until the damage is done. Conduit is built to deliver. When every guest message, regardless of property, platform, or time of day, is handled by an agent trained on the same SOPs and documentation, the variability that drives review score drift is removed at the source. The operations team monitors conversations through the Inbox and retains control; the AI handles the volume. That combination, reduced time spent on manual, repetitive messaging tasks paired with consistent quality at scale, is what makes the communication problem genuinely solvable as the portfolio grows. Essential Features to Look for in an Airbnb PMS: and the One Most Hosts Underweight That structural gap is exactly where PMS platforms separate. Two systems can look identical on a spec sheet and perform identically across a portfolio of three or four properties, then diverge sharply the moment listings multiply and message volume stops being manageable by one person on a good night's sleep. Channel Manager - Real-Time Calendar Sync A channel manager keeps your calendars across Airbnb, Vrbo, and Booking.com synchronized in real time so that a confirmed booking on one platform immediately blocks those dates everywhere else. Without it, the gap between a booking confirmation and the next iCal refresh is exactly where double bookings happen. A double booking doesn't just inconvenience hosts; it triggers automatic negative reviews, financial penalties, and potential account suspension. API-connected channel managers close that window entirely. iCal-based syncs do not. One pricing reality worth naming alongside calendar sync: hosts using a PMS are subject to Airbnb's fee model on their own terms. When a guest extends a reservation directly on Airbnb, the platform applies its own fee structure regardless of any markup a host has baked into their PMS-adjusted rates, meaning hosts can absorb Airbnb's cut out of their own earnings without ever choosing to. That silent financial loss compounds across a growing portfolio, and it's one more reason the architecture of your channel integration matters as much as whether sync is happening at all. Unified Inbox - One Dashboard for Every Guest Message A unified inbox pulls messages from Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, and direct channels into a single dashboard, so your team stops toggling between browser tabs to track who asked what. The operational benefit materializes most clearly at five or more properties, the point at which managing guest communications across multiple platforms simultaneously shifts from inconvenient to genuinely risky. A single missed thread at that scale turns into a 3-star review. Response time connects directly to Superhost status; Airbnb measures it precisely, and guests notice the difference between a ten-minute reply and one that arrives the next morning. This is where Conduit's Inbox is most beneficial: when your operation has scaled to the point where no single person can monitor every channel in real time. The Inbox gives your operations or support team one place to monitor, review, and manage all conversations, including the ones the AI agent is handling, so nothing falls through the gap between platforms. Dynamic Pricing Integration - Connecting Your PMS to Tools Like PriceLabs A PMS with native dynamic pricing integration connects to tools like PriceLabs so that rates adjust automatically based on demand signals, local events, and competitor availability. The trade-off worth naming: dynamic pricing tools require a calibration period, and operators who walk away in the first 30 days often leave money on the table before the algorithm has enough local data to work well. Scheduled templates handle anticipated messages, check-in instructions, WiFi codes, checkout reminders, and go silent the moment a guest sends something outside the queue. The most consequential PMS feature most hosts never evaluate is open API access to the messaging layer , not because it unlocks more templates, but because it determines whether an AI agent layer can ever be stacked on top. The real scaling question is whether the platform's architecture allows a purpose-built AI to inherit context, read SOPs, and resolve unscripted conversations that templates structurally cannot touch. Conduit's AI Agents are designed specifically for this layer. They are most beneficial when your business receives a high volume of repetitive guest messages and already has existing documentation, SOPs, FAQs, property manuals, to train the agent on. Critically, if that documentation already lives in tools like Notion or Google Drive, Conduit's Integrations pull from those sources directly, so there is no manual re-entry of content you have already written. Once connected, the AI agent delivers its first automated guest reply within days. From that point forward, it responds continuously, before, during, and after a stay, every time a guest sends a message, including the ones that land overnight or after hours when no one on your team is awake to catch them. Conduit's Workflows layer on top of that, triggering automated guest touchpoints after booking confirmation, check-in, or when a specific keyword is detected, so the predictable moments in a guest lifecycle stop requiring manual staff action entirely. The result is a communication architecture that scales with your portfolio rather than against it. 13 Best PMS for Airbnb Hosts to Manage More in 2026 Six platforms into a PMS comparison, most operators realize the feature lists start to blur. Calendar sync, unified inbox, automated templates, every serious tool on this list does those things. The real question is which platform fits your portfolio size today, your growth trajectory in 12 months, and the communication gaps that surface at 3 AM when no one is watching the inbox. The 13 picks below are organized around that decision, not a spec sheet. Each earns its slot for a specific operator profile. Read the tradeoff for each; that is where the real selection signal lives. 1. Conduit.ai - Best AI Guest Communication Layer for Airbnb Hosts The gap every PMS leaves open is not calendar sync or owner reporting, it is the unscripted mid-stay conversation that no template sequence was built to handle. Most operators running 15 or more properties discover this six months after their PMS goes live: the unified inbox is full, templates are firing on schedule, and the operations lead is still fielding 40 guest messages a day. Conduit's hospitality-specific AI agents sit on top of whichever PMS you already use, reading your own SOPs and FAQs to handle those conversations end-to-end. That is how Cash Flow Street, a 35-property portfolio, reached AI for hospitality , not by switching PMS platforms, but by adding the communication layer the PMS was never designed to replace. The AI agent layer earns its seat fastest when two conditions are both true: The portfolio already receives a high volume of repetitive guest messages. The operator has existing documentation, SOPs, FAQs, or property manuals, the agent can train on. Without that documentation as a ground-truth source, the agent cannot generate contextually accurate replies and the automation rate will be materially lower. 2. Guesty - Best Enterprise-Grade PMS for Scaling Airbnb Portfolios For large portfolios, typically 10 or more properties, Guesty delivers the most comprehensive all-in-one automation on this list. Its capabilities include: Multi-unit calendar management Owner financial reporting A robust open API Deep OTA integrations under one roof The tradeoff is cost and minimum commitment; smaller operators frequently find the per-listing fees steep before they have the booking revenue to justify them. Pick Guesty when your portfolio is already at scale, your team needs enterprise-grade reporting, and you can absorb a premium price in exchange for not stitching together five separate tools. 3. Hostaway - Best All-in-One PMS for Mid-Size Airbnb Operators Hostaway is a preferred software partner with Airbnb, Vrbo, and Booking.com, which translates to deeper OTA integrations and faster sync reliability than most mid-market alternatives. For growth-focused operators scaling from 5 to 50 properties, that partnership tier matters: rate updates push faster, calendar blocks resolve cleaner, and channel-specific promotions are easier to manage. The platform covers automated messaging, task management, and a direct booking website in one subscription. The honest limitation is that Hostaway's messaging automation relies on scheduled templates, it handles known touchpoints well but hands unscripted guest conversations back to your team. 4. Hospitable - Best Beginner-Friendly PMS for New Airbnb Hosts For the 1-to-3-property host who wants automation without a steep learning curve, Hospitable (formerly Smartbnb) is the clearest starting point. Its guest messaging automation is designed for Superhosts prioritizing fast response times and consistent communication quality, two factors Airbnb directly ties to Superhost status and search ranking. (Note: independent head-to-head benchmarks comparing Hospitable's response speed against alternatives are not publicly available; the response-time reputation rests largely on operator community feedback rather than verified third-party data, so testing during the trial period is the most reliable evaluation method.) The ceiling shows up around 10 properties, when the need for owner reporting, multi-channel distribution, and team task management outgrows what Hospitable was designed to do. 5. OwnerRez - Best PMS for Airbnb Hosts Who Want Deep Reporting and Direct Bookings OwnerRez is the power-user pick: direct booking website functionality, granular owner financial reporting, and workflow customization that experienced operators genuinely use. Hosts who have outgrown simpler tools and want to reduce OTA dependency find OwnerRez gives them the infrastructure to do it without hiring a developer. The tradeoff is a steeper setup curve, it rewards operators who invest time in configuration and punishes those who want plug-and-play. If deep customization matters more than fast onboarding, this is the right pick. 6. Hostfully - Best PMS for Versatile Property Managers Across Portfolio Sizes Hostfully occupies a useful middle ground: capable enough for operators at 10 to 30 properties, without the enterprise pricing floor that Guesty requires. Its digital guidebook feature is a genuine differentiator, reducing repetitive pre-arrival guest questions by surfacing property information before guests ask. The platform covers channel management, automated messaging, and owner reporting in a single interface. Operators who need highly customized reporting or complex multi-brand setups will hit the ceiling faster than they expect. 7. Lodgify - Best Website-First PMS for Airbnb Hosts Building Direct Booking Channels Lodgify is the clearest choice when reducing Airbnb fee exposure is the primary goal. Its direct booking website builder is purpose-built for operators who want a guest-facing brand presence, SEO control, and a commission-free reservation channel alongside their OTA listings, a focus that shapes where the platform invests its roadmap, though operators should verify current feature depth through the trial period before committing. The PMS layer covers calendar sync and basic automation, but Lodgify's real value is in the booking engine and website, not operational depth. Operators who need both will likely need a second tool. 8. Enso Connect - Best PMS Add-On for Centralizing Guest Messaging and Driving Upsells Enso Connect is a guest experience layer rather than a full PMS replacement, and it is most useful when stacked on top of an existing operational system. Its guest portal centralizes messaging, digital check-in, and upsell opportunities, early check-out fees, mid-stay add-ons, local experience packages, in a single guest-facing interface. Its messaging AI handles FAQ-style interactions well but does not autonomously resolve complex mid-stay requests or maintenance escalations without a human in the loop. It is a strong upsell and check-in tool; it is not a full communication automation solution. 9. PriceLabs - Best Dynamic Pricing Engine for Airbnb Revenue Optimization PriceLabs is not a PMS. It belongs on this list because no PMS's native pricing engine matches what a dedicated dynamic pricing tool delivers at scale. PriceLabs reads local demand signals, competitor rates, seasonality, and lead time to adjust nightly rates automatically, a function that materially affects revenue per available night for any portfolio above three properties. It integrates cleanly with Guesty, Hostaway, Hospitable, Uplisting, and most other platforms on this list. Operators who do not invest time in initial setup often leave the most impactful customizations unused. 10. Turno - Best Cleaning Operations Platform Integrated with Airbnb PMS Workflows Guest communication quality depends partly on what happens between checkouts. Turno (formerly TurnoverBnB) automates cleaner scheduling, sends photo checklists, and syncs turnover tasks directly with Airbnb reservation calendars, removing the manual coordination that causes delayed check-ins and the negative reviews that follow. For operators managing 5 or more properties with rotating cleaning teams, Turno reduces the coordination overhead that otherwise falls on the operations lead. It is not a PMS; it is the operations layer that keeps the physical property ready so the guest communication layer has nothing to apologize for. 11. Tokeet - Best Budget-Friendly PMS for Multi-Channel Airbnb Hosts on a Tight Margin Tokeet's pricing is its headline advantage: one of the most affordable multi-channel PMS options for hosts managing several properties across Airbnb, Vrbo, and Booking.com simultaneously. For operators who need calendar sync and a unified inbox without a large monthly commitment, Tokeet delivers the core functionality. The caution worth surfacing: operators who have used Tokeet at scale report frustration with customer support responsiveness and difficulty modifying plans. If budget is the primary constraint and you are comfortable with a self-serve support experience, Tokeet is a reasonable starting point, but test it thoroughly before committing to an annual plan. 12. iGMS - Best Automation-Focused PMS for Airbnb Superhosts Managing Multiple Accounts Superhosts who have split listings across separate Airbnb profiles, for different brand identities, co-hosting arrangements, or ownership structures, find iGMS handles the consolidation cleanly. Its automated messaging and task management cover the core PMS functions, and the multi-account architecture is genuinely useful for operators in that situation. The platform is less competitive on owner financial reporting and direct booking infrastructure compared to OwnerRez or Hostfully. 13. Rentals United - Best Channel Manager for Airbnb Hosts Distributing Across 60+ OTAs Rentals United is the right tool when distribution breadth is the constraint, not operational management. Connecting inventory to a large number of OTAs simultaneously, including niche channels most full-service PMS platforms do not reach natively, is Rentals United's primary differentiator; operators targeting specialty booking platforms or global markets should verify current channel availability directly with the vendor, as integration counts change with platform updates. For operators building occupancy across global markets or targeting specialty booking platforms alongside Airbnb, the channel reach justifies the added subscription. Most operators using it pair it with a separate PMS, such as Smoobu or OwnerRez, for task management, owner reporting, and guest communication. Every platform above solves a different slice of the operational puzzle, but knowing which one fits your portfolio today is only half the decision. The other half is knowing which combination of tools will still hold as you add your next ten properties, which is exactly what the next section maps out. Airbnb PMS - Choosing by Portfolio Size and Growth Stage Portfolio size tells you which PMS tier to start on. It doesn't tell you when you'll outgrow it, or what breaks first when you do. The sharpest operators treat portfolio size as one variable in a two-part equation, with the second variable being the communication ceiling their chosen platform will eventually hit. Tier 1 (1 to 3 Properties): Prioritize Simplicity and Automation Depth Feature count is a distraction at this stage. What matters is how deeply the platform automates the touchpoints you actually send every booking: pre-arrival instructions, check-in codes, checkout reminders, and review requests. A tool that executes those sequences reliably, without manual intervention, is worth more than one with forty integrations you won't use for two years. Complexity at this tier creates maintenance overhead solo operators can't absorb. One thing beginners consistently underestimate: when Airbnb adjusts its fee model, most PMS setups offer no automatic recalibration of pricing strategy. Hosts are left manually reconciling platform fee changes against their listed rates, a gap that quietly erodes competitiveness. This is a solvable problem, but only if the tools you choose from the start are designed to connect to existing content and platforms without manual re-entry. Conduit's Integrations layer addresses this directly: if you're already working out of Notion, Google Drive, or Airbnb itself, the AI agent pulls from that content without requiring you to rebuild anything from scratch. Tier 2 (5 to 20 Properties): Evaluate Growth Platforms on API Openness, Not Just Channel Count The failure point at this tier is almost never channel coverage; it's integration flexibility. An operator projecting 25 properties in 18 months who locks into a closed platform discovers too late that adding dynamic pricing or a guest communication layer requires an enterprise upgrade or a full migration. Before signing, ask specifically whether the API supports read and write access for guest message threads, not just calendar data. This is also the tier where communication volume begins compounding faster than headcount can absorb it. The experience of operators like Easy BnB is instructive: 14 virtual assistants running 24/7 guest coverage, with 80% of that communication volume consisting of low-value, repetitive exchanges, questions about check-in, WiFi, and checkout timing. That labor model dragged margins and capped EBITDA, directly limiting exit valuation. Staff reliability issues compounded the problem. The lesson isn't that you need more staff at Tier 2. It's that locking into a PMS without a clear path to an AI communication layer means you're building toward that same labor trap. Conduit's AI Agents are most beneficial precisely at this inflection point: when incoming message volume is high, repetitive, and documentable, and when you have SOPs or FAQs that can train the agent within days of connecting your materials. Tier 3 (20 Plus Properties): Enterprise PMS Criteria Per-property pricing that looks reasonable at 10 listings can become a structural cost problem at 50. Operators who don't model the per-unit cost gap before signing annual contracts often face a renegotiation they weren't budgeting for. Annual lock-in before volume testing is one of the most common regret patterns among operators who scale past 20 properties. Demand monthly billing or a volume-step pricing schedule before committing. At this scale, the staffing math becomes existential. Enabling rapid portfolio expansion without proportional growth in support headcount isn't a nice-to-have; it's the difference between a scalable business and one that's permanently labor-constrained. The short-term rental market has grown significantly , and operators who reach 20-plus listings without solving the communication throughput problem find themselves unable to grow further without adding costly headcount at every step. Conduit's Inbox gives operations and support teams a single surface to monitor, review, and manage all conversations the AI agent is handling across every property and platform simultaneously, without scaling the team in proportion to the portfolio. Does Your PMS Support an AI Communication Layer? Every PMS tier was architected to reduce calendar, scheduling, and operational friction. None were designed to eliminate the human in the loop on guest communication. When a host crosses roughly 15 listings, two crises compound simultaneously: a PMS migration event and a communication throughput problem the new platform's native automation still cannot solve. Hosts at this inflection point frequently misdiagnose the staffing problem as a PMS selection problem, switching platforms without fixing the actual bottleneck. The right framing, articulated clearly by operators who've been through this: AI-first is the right approach. The operators who try to build bespoke communication tooling on top of a PMS, or who rely on VA networks to fill the gap, consistently discover that purpose-built AI does it better, at lower marginal cost, and without the reliability risk of human shift coverage. Conduit's Workflows layer is designed for exactly the recurring, predictable touchpoints that currently require manual staff action: triggered automatically after a booking is confirmed, after check-in, or when a specific keyword surfaces in a guest conversation. The first automated guest reply goes live days after connecting your existing SOPs and manuals, not weeks, and not after a lengthy onboarding process. Scheduled templates cover the predictable moments. They go silent on everything else. Open API access to the messaging layer determines whether an AI agent can ever sit on top of your PMS and inherit the context it needs to resolve unscripted conversations, which means selecting a PMS based on native automation quality sets a ceiling, not a floor. And as the Cash Flow Street and Easy BnB outcomes show, the ROI from an AI agent layer only materializes when the PMS beneath it provides real-time messaging hooks and the operator already has documented SOPs to train on. Together, those two conditions point to one concrete next step: mapping an AI communication layer to the PMS you have already chosen, using the documentation you have already written. Start by exploring AI for hospitality at conduit.ai, where Conduit's agents connect to your existing SOPs, FAQs, and property manuals to handle unscripted guest conversations end-to-end, across every channel, without adding headcount or switching platforms. Frequently Asked Questions Does a PMS actually handle guest messages automatically, or does someone still have to reply? A PMS automates scheduled, predictable messages, check-in instructions, WiFi codes, checkout reminders, but goes silent the moment a guest sends something outside those templates. Unscripted questions, mid-stay issues, and overnight messages still land in an inbox waiting for a human to read and reply. An AI agent layer like conduit.ai sits on top of your existing PMS to handle those open-ended conversations end-to-end, including ones that arrive at 2 a.m. How does dynamic pricing actually work inside a PMS, and is there a catch? A PMS with dynamic pricing integration connects to tools like PriceLabs so that rates adjust automatically based on demand signals, local events, and competitor availability. The catch the post flags is a required calibration period, operators who disconnect within the first 30 days often leave money on the table before the algorithm has enough local data to perform well. At what portfolio size does managing guest messages manually actually break down? The post points to five or more properties as the threshold where a unified inbox stops being convenient and starts being operationally critical, a single missed thread at that scale can turn into a 3-star review. By 15 to 20 listings, daily message volume stops being a communication task and becomes a full-time job, with operators spending 20 or more minutes per booking on routine exchanges like WiFi passwords and parking instructions. Why does slow or inconsistent guest messaging hurt my Airbnb ranking, not just my reviews? Airbnb requires a 90% or higher response rate within 24 hours to qualify for Superhost status, and its guidance confirms that response time directly affects search ranking and booking conversion. The post describes this as a revenue problem that compounds silently, booking by booking, until the review score reflects it, meaning the overnight gap costs money even when no guest explicitly complains. What should I actually check when evaluating whether a PMS can support AI-powered guest communication later? The post identifies open API access to the messaging layer as the most consequential feature most hosts never evaluate, not because it unlocks more templates, but because it determines whether an AI agent can ever be stacked on top. The architecture question is whether the platform allows a purpose-built AI to inherit context, read your SOPs, and resolve unscripted conversations that templates structurally cannot touch.

title: The Best Side Support Bras (2026)
summary: Side bra spillage isn't always a cup-size issue. Learn how side-panel construction improves support and which Honeylove bra best fits your needs.
body_text: The CloudEmbrace also comes in a CloudWire version ($79) for readers who want the same smooth wing construction with added underwire structure. The CloudWire wraps a flexible wire in light foam for zero wire-to-skin contact. What reviewers say: Across 224 reviews (4.1 stars) , reviewers call the CloudEmbrace their most comfortable bra, often contrasting it directly with painful or digging underwire they wore for years. Several say it stays put under fitted tops without a single adjustment all day. Best for: Readers whose side tissue issue is caused by conventional bra seams and edges digging in and creating a spill effect. Especially suited to anyone with sensitivity to structure at the sides, those who find standard bra wings irritating, and those who need a completely smooth, invisible side profile under fitted tops and jersey fabrics. #3 Leonisa High Profile Back Smoothing Bra: Best for maximum side and back coverage with flexible side boning Leonisa's High Profile bra takes a tall-and-wide approach to side coverage. The cups are taller than a standard T-shirt bra, enclosing more of the upper bust and side zone. The wings are reinforced with flexible boning channels: vertical structure built into the side panels that holds the wing upright and prevents it from collapsing laterally throughout the day. For the reader whose main issue is uncovered real estate between the cup edge and the underarm, this bra covers more of that zone than most wireless options on the market. Features and pricing: $60; bands 34-40, cups B-DD/E High-profile cup construction covers more of the upper bust and side area Wide wings with flexible boning channels prevent wing rolldown and lateral collapse Wireless construction Full back coverage: wide band designed to smooth back and side at once What reviewers say: The high-coverage side and back panels draw repeat praise for smoothing visible texture under clothing. Reviewers cite "excellent support" as the most common theme, and many call it the best bra for side and back smoothing they have found. A consistent minority find the side-boning support bars uncomfortable, describing digging or pain after a few hours. Scattered reports mention oversized padding and friction with the return process. Honest tradeoff: A recurring complaint pattern across reviews is that the flexible boning bars in the side panels cause discomfort or digging after extended wear, particularly during seated activity or when the bra shifts position. Readers with side sensitivity or a history of boning-related discomfort should weigh this carefully. Best for: Readers who need maximum height and width of side coverage, particularly women who find that standard bras leave the entire upper side and underarm zone uncovered. Best suited to daily wear where the bra stays mostly stationary. #4 Glamorise MagicLift Natural Shape Support Bra (Style 1010): Best wireless option for extended sizing with higher side panels This is the extended-sizing pick in this roundup. Side spillage intensifies at larger cup volumes, and most of the other bras on this list stop well short of the sizes where that problem gets worst. The Glamorise 1010 reaches bands 36-50 and cups B-I. Its higher side panels are designed to reduce underarm spillage, a feature called out directly by reviewers and confirmed in the product construction. Features and pricing: $59; bands 36-50, cups B-I (the widest size range on this list) Wireless construction Higher side panels engineered to reduce underarm spillage Diagonal seam for rounded, natural shape support Full-cup coverage Cushioned straps designed to distribute weight without digging What reviewers say: Reviewers in larger cup sizes (F through I) consistently praise the Glamorise 1010 as one of the only wire-free bras that delivers real lift and support, often after years of relying on underwire. Several call out cushioned straps that do not dig into the shoulders. Multiple reviewers with uneven breast tissue say the fit evens out the difference better than any other bra they have tried. A number of longtime customers say they have replaced their entire underwire collection with this style. Sizing consistency is the top complaint. Several reviewers say the band-to-cup ratio runs tight or unpredictable. A smaller group, mostly in the largest cups, say the lift does not hold up by the end of the day. Honest tradeoff: Women in larger cup sizes (42G and above) report a recurring pattern: the bra rolls, the lift drops, and the side panels lose position throughout the day. This is not universal, but it is significant enough that readers in 42G+ cups who need firm side containment should consider it a risk. Best for: Readers in extended sizes, particularly bands 40-50, who need higher side panel coverage and cannot find that construction in the standard size range. Strongest pick for light-to-moderate support needs in the B-F cup range. Not the strongest pick for readers in 42G+ cups who need firm containment all day. #5 Bali One Smooth U Ultra Light Underwire Bra (Style DF3439): Best affordable underwire option for light side smoothing This bra serves a specific reader: someone who wants underwire support alongside side smoothing and is shopping at a lower price point. The smooth wing construction and flush cup-to-side transition are designed to reduce visible texture under clothing. It is the only underwire pick in this lineup, and it earns its spot for the reader who is not ready to go wireless but wants a cleaner side profile than her current underwire delivers. Features and pricing: $54 (often on sale for $25.99); bands 32-42, cups B-DDD Traditional underwire for structured lift and support Smooth wing panels designed for a clean side profile under clothing Ultra-light fabric construction Tagless finish What reviewers say: Long-time repeat customers, some loyal for 15-plus years, consistently praise the comfort and soft fabric as the reason they keep choosing it. Several say it is the rare underwire that does not dig or poke. Multiple customers mention owning eight or more in different colors and reordering on a regular cycle. Two negative patterns stand out: several longtime wearers say the sizing has recently shrunk, and others report underwire poking through or straps popping loose within months of regular wear. Honest tradeoff: Recent reviews contain a recurring pattern of sizing inconsistency and underwire durability, with multiple reviewers reporting underwire poking through the fabric within one to four months of regular wear. Sizing up one band and ordering in advance of need to account for potential returns is worth considering. Best for: Readers who want underwire support alongside light side smoothing at a limited budget (especially when on sale). Suits light side-smoothing needs under everyday clothing. Not suited to readers who need active containment of significant side tissue or who have had negative experiences with underwire durability. Give your breasts the side support they deserve with Honeylove bras Side spillage is a construction problem. Specifically, it is a side-panel construction problem. The right solution depends on the root cause: a bra with no lateral structure, seam edges that dig in and push tissue outward, or wings too narrow and short to cover the migration zone. The Honeylove CrossOver Bra solves it with a wraparound crossover panel and flexible side boning that holds tissue in place from outside the cup to the underarm. The Honeylove CloudEmbrace Bra solves it with bonded raw-cut wing edges that eliminate the raised seam lines and dig-in points that push side tissue outward in the first place. Both are available in bands 30-44, cups A-G, and both ship with free returns. Use Honeylove's bra size calculator to confirm your fit before ordering, and try the CrossOver or CloudEmbrace without commitment. Shop bestsellers Side support bra FAQs Side support is one of the most misunderstood areas of bra fit. Often, side spillage is caused by a construction issue, not a sizing error. Below are answers to the questions that come up most often about side spillage, bra construction, and finding the right fix. What is a side support bra? A side support bra is built with wider, taller wings and structured side panels that hold breast tissue inside the cup and prevent it from migrating toward the underarm. Unlike standard bras that rely on cup volume alone, side support bras use construction features like flexible boning, extended panel height, or bonded edges to actively manage lateral tissue. Why does tissue push out the sides of my bra even when the cup fits? Because the cup might fit the front projection of the breast while the side panel is too narrow, too short, or too soft to contain lateral tissue. Breast tissue is mobile, and gravity pulls it sideways throughout the day. Without structured side coverage, the tissue migrates past the cup edge and creates a visible ridge under clothing. Does sizing up in the cup fix side spillage? Not typically. Sizing up adds volume to the front of the cup without changing the side panel construction. The result is often a cup that gaps at the front while the tissue still spills at the sides. The fix is a bra with taller wing height, firmer lateral panels, or bonded edges designed to hold tissue in from the side. What bra features actually prevent side spillage? Three construction features matter most for side containment: Taller wing height that extends coverage from the cup edge toward the underarm Flexible side boning or structured panels that prevent the wing from collapsing and hold tissue in place Bonded or raw-cut wing edges that eliminate the raised seam ridges that dig in and push tissue outward

title: What Is Demo Software? Types & Top Tools for 2026
summary: The five types of demo software, plus a comparison of top demo tools like Navattic, Testbox, and Arcade.
body_text: The rise of PLG has prompted an explosion of new tools and strategies designed to help customers get hands-on with a product faster. Demo software is any tool that lets go-to-market teams show a product to buyers without a rep walking through it live through pre-built interactive tours, recorded video, sandbox environments, or an AI agent that navigates the product and answers questions on its own. In fact, this area has grown so quickly that one of G2's fastest-growing categories is demo automation. What is demo software? Demo software is any no-code tool that lets go-to-market teams put their product in front of buyers without a rep manually walking them through it every time. Teams typically combine five formats, depending on where a buyer is in their journey: Live demos – a rep walks through the real product on a call. Pre-recorded demos - a video or slide deck that shows key flows. Interactive demos - a clickable tour that runs on its own and lets buyers explore at their pace. Sandbox demos - live, interactive product environments that SEs use to showcase various features during a demo call. AI agent demos - a conversational AI agent that navigates the product live, answers buyer questions in real time, and adapts the walkthrough based on what they ask. It can be used as demo automation for high-level overviews of your product so your team can spend more time customizing and personalizing demos for their highest-value accounts. What are the types of sales demo software? Most simple interactive demos take 15 to 30 minutes to capture, edit, and publish. More detailed, branched, or sandbox demos usually fit into a few hours. Below, we define each of them and share where they typically sit in the sales cycle: 1. Live demos Live demos are conducted one-on-one with a prospect, where sales engineers and AEs review the product in detail. Oftentimes, they show product functionality in a full-copy sandbox while prospects watch and listen as the presenter shares their screen, pointing out various features depending on what issues a prospect is facing. The downside to live demos is that they are tough to scale. Unlike an interactive demo, which users can access at any time, a live demo still requires a rep to guide them through it. Sandbox demos , however, can be a good happy medium. Rather than building a live environment from scratch for every call, SEs can create reusable, configurable demos that feel real and prevent technical hiccups. Best for: 1:1 sales meetings, particularly during upsell and expansion calls. 2. Pre-recorded videos Videos and still shots of your product generate awareness among prospects and get them to consider your tool as a contender in their evaluation. They can be reused in multiple sales conversations, marketing materials, or onboarding resources, and they can address a large audience. At the same time, videos are more passive and harder to personalize. They don’t give prospects the opportunity to get hands-on with your product, and they can’t be edited like HTML/CSS data, making it hard to clean up messy product data. Not to mention, high-end product videos can be costly; they have to be updated with each new feature or UI release. Best for: Blog posts, help centers 3. Interactive demos Interactive demos are click-through, guided product experiences embedded on websites or shared via email. They showcase product capabilities and empower potential buyers to experience the product before they buy it. Plus, interactive demos can be edited and tailored specifically for each ICP, guiding prospects straight to aha moments that prompt conversion. Interactive product demo software captures HTML/CSS data so it looks and feels like your actual product. HTML/ CSS captures can also be easily edited to fit demo requirements or blur out unfinished UI or messy product data. And because they’re no-code, any member of the GTM team can spin up a new one in just a few days. Best for: Your website, sales leave-behinds, champion enablement and in-app activation 4. Sandbox demos Sandbox demos are simulated environments of your product that reps can use to demo live, but aren't the real thing. They are built for reusability: SEs only have to create and customize them once, and then can reuse them until features change. Because there’s no risk of broken flows, last-minute bugs, or integration issues, sandbox demos are ideal when you may not have good wifi, presenting a new product, or are showing off a more complex workflow or integration. Best for: Conferences, in-person meetings, multi-product use cases 5. AI agent demos Unlike a pre-built interactive tour, an AI agent demo runs live: it greets the buyer, asks what they want to see, and moves through the product in real time, answering questions as if a rep were on the call. It's the newest category in demo software, and it's growing fast enough that most vendors on this list now offer some version of it. Best for: Qualifying inbound leads 24/7, self-serve exploration of complex products, and answering buyer edge-case questions without an SE on the call. Top Sales Demo Platforms Research methodology We gathered insights from G2 reviews, Reddit threads, and interviews with actual buyers who evaluated demo software during vendor comparisons. All quotes are directly sourced from public reviews and Navattic customer case studies. Tool Best For G2 Rating Ease of Use Software Demo Type Navattic GTM teams scaling top-of-funnel, AEs + SEs sending 1-to-1 demos 4.8 Extremely easy Interactive demos, video, ai agent demos, sandboxes TestBox Hands-on product evaluation with real data 4.8 Moderate Live demos Reprise Pre-sales teams building complex, custom demo environments 4.4 Steep learning curve Interactive demos, live demos, sandboxes Arcade Marketing teams creating light, engaging product walkthroughs 4.7 Very easy Video + screenshot demos Consensus Enterprise SE teams supporting large-scale evaluations 4.8 Moderate Video demos, interactive demos, ai agent demos Walnut Sales teams needing reusable demo flows with personalization 4.5 Moderate Interactive demos, live demos DemoStack Technical SEs replicating full product environments 4.7 High complexity Live demos, interactive demos, sandbox Navattic Type: Interactive Demo, Sandbox Demos, AI Agent Demos Navattic's Launchpad demo automation software lets sales reps send early-stage prospects async demos before and after live calls and save presales time from unqualified calls. With Navattic, any team member can create HTML/CSS automated interactive demos that look and feel like your actual software without engineering help. Our product supports interactive demo builds for mobile apps, desktop apps, and other web-based tools. Navattic's AI agents run inside a clone of your demo environment, guiding and qualifying prospects, answering questions in their own words, and routing qualified leads to sales with the context AEs need, in any language. Teams can monitor agent talk time and engagement on the backend to see which conversations are driving the strongest buyer interest. Try an interactive demo of Navattic Pros Easy to share. “As an AE, what I appreciate most about Navattic is how easy it is to share interactive product demos. It's a great way to let prospects experience value upfront - especially early in the sales cycle.” ( from ProductBoard ) Has the complexity SE teams need. “Navattic was our winner [for a click through demo tool]: Best end-to-end analytics, support for multi-branch click-throughs, price includes CSM (no separate fee), great to work with.” ( r/salesengineers ) Makes demoing accessible to every team member. “Navattic allows us to build guided demos to allow any of our sales team to run a demo without always needing an SE on the call to do a live demo - this helps with scale and time/bandwidth constraints. The building experience makes it quick to build demos (and customise/adjust the UI) and then offer a variety of consumption modes, such as demo with text boxes for a fully guided experience, and then the ability to toggle these off for a more presenter-type mode (pseudo-live demo).” ( G2 ) Cons Live demo options. We can't create a full demo environment replica, but we do have the ability to create high-level “click-anywhere” sandboxes. Terminology : Some users report a bit of a learning curve when it comes to interactive demo technology, like flows, captures, modals, and tooltips ( G2 ). Pricing Navattic has five pricing plans : Starter: $0/month, which comes with 1 seat, 1 demo (HTML or media), unlimited demo views, and basic analytics. Startup: $125/month, which comes with 1 seat, unlimited HTML demos, the MCP server, Navattic JS, custom themes, and checklists. Base, at $500 per month, gets you 5 seats, unlimited HTML demos, Salesforce, Marketo, and 25+ other integrations, account identification, sandbox demos, A/B testing, and a dedicated CSM. Growth, at $1,000 per month, gets you 10 seats, sales integrations (Gong, Salesloft, Outreach, Gmail, Outlook, and more), interest level demos, buyer circle discovery, demo translation, custom domains, and SSO and directory sync. Enterprise: Talk to sales, comes with all Growth plan features, plus custom seats, offline demos, HTML capture translation, audit logs, professional services, priority support, and demo consultation. Testbox Type: Sandbox demo Pros Intuitive UI. “TestBox enables our organization and team to automate manual processes and scale end-user experiences with our platform. The UI is intuitive and easy to use for our less technical teams and customers.” ( G2 ) Great support. “The service/support. Any time I have an issue, new request, question etc., our dedicated Solutions Eng. responds on Slack immediately, and ensures he addresses my comment ASAP.” ( G2 ) Cons Missing reporting functionality. “Not all features and functionality are available within testbox. So there are a couple instances where you have to have the other demo tool open so you can showcase different things.” ( G2 ) Hard to edit yourself. “We are discouraged from editing the testbox account (creating new numbers, editing call flows, etc.). It would be great to be able to do all of this and have the account automatically delete any changes as to show how it works practically to clients.” ( G2 ) Pricing Testbox has 3 pricing plans: Startup: $44,750 for 15 users. Comes with a single, foundational demo or POC experience (no integrations). Growth: $59,500 for 15 users. Comes with multiple product modules, complex data-driven workflows, and third-party integrations. Enterprise: Contact sales. Comes with the ability to show interconnected product suites, AI-powered workflows, and covers advanced data requirements and segmentation needs. Each additional user is $1,200/year. Reprise Type: Interactive Demo, Sandbox Demo Pros Supports both live and guided demos. “I like that you can use Reprise to build live demos as well as self-guided demos without writing any lines of code. For custom changes, you could just modify HTML and CSS.” ( G2 ) Good for technical pre-sales teams. “I was asked to develop a quick 10-15 min demo for our platform. Without much training, only a guided 1-hour session with another coworker who has used it, I made it work. I delivered my 10 min demo and my audience was happy.” ( G2 ) Cons Higher setup time for live environments. “It is a comprehensive product with growing configurability. So the trade-off is, to utilize all of its features, all of its capabilities, it takes time to learn. There are some rather more technical pieces to it as well that require more specialized knowledge.” ( G2 ) Can be resource-intensive to maintain. “The demo experience itself can still use some refinement to make it more app-like. Some features, such as hiding certain elements or working with modals, require custom code, which means engineering time with Reprise.” ( G2 ) Pricing Contact sales. According to Vendr, the median buyer pays $28,000 per year . Arcade Type: Video + Screenshot Pros Ease of use. Users say things like: “Very simple and intuitive experience do record and edit a demo. The setup was really quick as well. And also I didn't need to reach any person of the support or cs team to get things done,” ( G2 ) and “Arcade is easy to use and what we did was create interactive demos for various use cases/industries.” ( Reddit ) Quick support. “I've also been impressed with the quick support provided by their team when I've researched best practices or reached out with questions.” ( G2 ) Cons Screenshot-based, making editing difficult. Users say things like, “It can be a bit fiddly getting into the way of using it in terms of cropping videos and editing” and “ Adding additional scenes into an Arcade can sometimes feel clunky - there's a lot of copy pasting and tabs open.” ( G2 , G2 ) Limited recording availability. “I don't like that the recording feature is limited to the web browser, as we often have to record things outside the browser (desktop applications, etc.).” ( G2 ) Pricing Arcade has 4 cost tiers: Free: $0/month. Comes with 1 user, 3 published Arcades, chapters, background music, synthetic voiceover, and camera recording. Pro: $32/month for 1 user. Comes with unlimited Arcades, removed Arcade watermark, Global Insights, blur, video editing, pan and zoom, and GIF/video export. Growth: $42.50/month per user. Comes with white-labeled Arcades, custom themes, collections, Advanced Insights, advanced branching, advanced permissions, Audience Reveal, Forms, integrations, translations, and commenting. Enterprise: Talk to sales, minimum 10 users. HTML Capture, version control, SSO, Insights exports, custom domain, demo services, advanced onboarding, dedicated CSM support, API, and a private Slack channel. Consensus Type: Video demos, interactive demos Pros Solid analytics. “The analytics provide valuable insight into what each stakeholder has viewed, which features they care about most, and how engaged they are. It helps me prioritize and tailor outreach more effectively.” ( G2 ) High rep adoption. “I enjoy using Consensus videos to introduce myself and my product to a prospect or share a specific function of my product as a follow-up in the sales process.” ( G2 ) Cons Limited branching. “One major drawback is the inability to link to a single video for multiple features. This limitation forces us to upload the same video repeatedly for each feature, which is time-consuming and inefficient.” ( G2 ) Primarily video-based. Users say things like, “I'd like to see a more SharePoint like interface with storing video/demo assets. Having to interact and upload videos through the GUI every time can become slow and tedious. They need a file share style engagement portal with the video content,” and “If I add multiple demos to a board, even with an intro video letting them know there are multiple demos, they still only watch the first. So I am still sending multiple demos and having to be creative in how I deliver that.” ( G2 , G2 ) Pricing Contact sales. According to their pricing page, cost depends on role and license quantity. Walnut Type: Interactive demo, Sandbox Demo Pros Supports personalized demos for sales teams. “I love how customizable Walnut is, allowing you to open the door to prospects, enabling them to really see what the solution would look like and work for their specific company.” ( G2 ) Story Capture lets salespeople transform their regular talk track into a guided interactive demo. Playlists allow Walnut users to create a curated set of demos, content assets, and links to share with prospects or customers. Cons Limited support for mobile apps. Walnut’s Chrome extension only works on web-based products. Users say, “Support for mobile apps is a little convoluted, but they seem to be working on it,” (G2) and “We had some difficulty building Walnut demos from a mobile point of view because the platform only allows us to take screen captures from a web browser.” ( G2 ) It can be buggy. Users say things like, “The multi-resolution mode frequently messes up my browser window when I try to use it,” ( G2 ) and “Sometimes the preview is different than what it actually captured and then in later stages when we open it in Edit mode, the screen shows different which is a big downside. When changing the selected element for the tooltip, you need to give a couple of tries.” ( G2 ) Pricing Walnut has three pricing plans for its interactive demo platform: Ignite: $750/month for 3 seats. Accelerate: $1,550/month for 5 editor seats, 5 presenter seats. Comes with: sandbox demos, prospect personalization, video overlays, Sales & Customer Hub Playlists, advanced analytics, Walnut Uncover, and an advanced Salesforce integration. Enterprise: Contact sales, custom seats. Comes with: SSO & SCIM, white-labeled brand experience, and advanced language localization. They also charge separately for interactive deal rooms at $70 per user per month. Or, if you want to consolidate deal rooms and interactive demos, you can get up to 10 seats for $35 per user per month. Demostack Type: Sandbox demos, Interactive demos Pros Powerful for technical and sandbox-style demos. “[Being able to] change the look and themes of what I'm showing proves that we listen and understand customer challenges. Demostack is fine for SDRs and downmarket AEs who want to show a high-level overview but not to scale complex demo scenarios.” ( G2 ) Steeper learning curve. “I wish the demo URL would not change if I edited something in the demo, it's a bit troublesome to update it in the many resources that use it. title: What AI-Native Research Actually Looks Like: Lessons from Calendly and Included Health
body_text: Blog Posts August 19, 2026 What AI-Native Research Actually Looks Like: Lessons from Calendly and Included Health Contributors: Mahad Bullo Staff UX Researcher Staff UX Researcher at Included Health Ray Mason-Murillo Research Operations Manager Research Operations Manager at Calendly Recruitment has been the last piece of the research process to change. Planning, moderation, synthesis, analysis: all of it has been reshaped by AI over the past two years. Recruitment stayed stuck, and has been synonymous for pulling lists, managing spreadsheets, writing screeners, sending mail merges, chasing booking links, assigning NDAs, and mailing gift cards. For some teams that is ten or more tools for one study, and each step carries it’s own governance risk: PII moving between systems, consent that has to be captured, tax obligations on incentives, and participants who can be overcontacted by a stakeholder who meant to email 50 people and emailed 1,000. That risk used to be manageable because access was narrow, but that’s no longer the case with the building products becoming increasingly democratized. Product roles are blending, and stakeholders across the org now want direct user access. The question every Research and Research Ops team is facing: how do you keep the quality bar high without giving up speed, compliance, or participant experience? That is why we built Rally Agent and Rally MCP , both now open in beta. Rally MCP puts Rally's tools inside the agentic systems your company already uses: Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot. Rally Agent is an out-of-the-box research ops recruitment agent available in Slack, Claude, and in Rally's new agentic interface. Both sit on top of the same research infrastructure we have spent four years building, which means your permissions, templates, governance rules, approval workflows, and role types carry over completely. If someone can't launch recruitment in Rally, they can't launch it through the agent. If someone can't see PII in Rally, they can't see it through the MCP. Nothing destructive happens without a human approving it first. The philosophy is simple: the human work in research stays human. Everything else gets assisted or automated. And the agent doesn't draw the line on who can do what. You do. At our launch webinar, we brought on two customers who have been living inside this for months: Mahad Bullo , Senior Staff Researcher at Included Health, and Ray Mason-Murillo , the first Research Ops hire at Calendly. Here is what they told us. Research is already democratized. The question is whether it's governed. At Included Health , researchers, designers, and PMs all run research, with Rally acting as what Mahad calls the “nerve center” of their practice. Since adopting Rally, the team has 4x'd its research volume. Governance carries extra weight in healthcare, where HIPAA and PHI protections are not optional, and Included Health covers 84 million lives. Calendly had the opposite starting problem. Plenty of people were doing research when Ray arrived, but you’d have been hard pressed to find out about any of it. There was no central visibility and no tracking of volume at all. So while Ray can’t say whether volume went up, he’s seen a major improvement in study quality resulting in the team trusting insights more than ever before. Product managers, designers, and go-to-market folks are still running their own research, just more responsibly and with higher visibility across the organization. "AI native" means something different depending on where you sit For Ray, it means getting out of the enablement bottleneck. He used to be the person cleaning up study titles and teaching everyone the naming conventions and indexing standards. Now a designer or PM describes a study, the agent names and structures it the way Ray taught it, and the cleanup work goes away. For Mahad, it means asking what was impossible before. His example: connect a participant in Rally to their Marvin interview and their Maze prototype results, and suddenly mixed-method work is accessible to people who were never trained in those methods. Same for reporting, where skills let his team produce anything from a quick single-interview insight to a full readout, faster and in more layers. Both landed in the same place on the interface. Mahad said he could not remember the last time he opened the Rally UI, other than a call with his CSM the day before, as he’s been working almost exclusively through the MCP. The first thing each of them tested Mahad went straight to building a study from a plan. It worked, so he went into Rally to check whether it had actually captured everything and found that it had. From there he chained Rally's MCP to Sprig's and wrote a skill so that creating a Rally study also creates the in-product prompt. One less thing to remember on every study. He is now pointing the same approach at panel health. Building the panel was the exciting part. Managing it over time is the part that gets overwhelming, and that is where he expects the MCP to earn its keep. Ray started somewhere completely different, which he flagged live as a difference in how the two of them think about Research Ops. His pressing problem was a disorganized research repository, so he tested search. Pick a research topic, return the prior studies and specific interviews that match using transcript search, flag the strong matches, and say plainly when something looks like new territory. It came back fast and accurate with almost no fine-tuning. He checked the results himself, and they held up. His reaction: this does not feel like a V1. Where they see their roles going Ray is moving from doing research operations to enabling it. His 6 to 12 month goal is C-suite access: executives using plain language in Claude to access prior research without feeling like they are in the weeds. Meeting them where they already work, rather than asking them to learn a new tool they will never open. Mahad wants two things: first, a formal education and enablement program, which he named as a real gap at Included Health and one he thinks standardized skills and MCP workflows finally make possible. Second, deeper mixed-method work: an observability layer built with the data science team that follows a customer across Rally, Amplitude, and product usage, feeding data-rooted personas that Rally can then recruit against. He’s already running three to four studies a week with the team behind one of their flagship products, answering everything from ID card copy to bigger strategic questions. The point he keeps making internally is that research is not the slog product teams remember. The infrastructure exists so teams can spin up a study, recruit from the panel, and report out quickly. The old mental model is the thing that needs dislodging. The line that summed it up When governance is built into the agent, you stop worrying about whether someone is going to break a rule, because the rule is already embedded. Research and Research Ops teams are the ones positioned to architect the systems that let research scale safely. Rally Agent and MCP are the tools for building them. Rally Agent and Rally MCP are open in beta. If you're a customer, reach out to your CSM to get access. If you're not, get in touch and we'll set up a deep dive. ‍ No items found.
